name: Battle of Hillsbrad

meta.next: Battle of Hillsbrad (7) (Classic) (Classic) or Battle of Hillsbrad (7) (WotLK Classic)

summary: In Hillsbrad, the Forsaken turn their campaign on Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia sends Horde champions to break the dwarven garrison aiding local humans and kill its commander, Captain Ironhill.

sections.title: Testing the Alliance
sections.body: High Executor Darthalia has already pressed the human farmers and town militia across the foothills. Now she turns Tarren Mill's fury on Ironforge's troops. Dwarven soldiers have taken up arms for Southshore, strengthening the human presence in Lordaeron. Darthalia sees that alliance as an obstacle to be broken. She means to show the Alliance that helping the human survivors will bring devastation.

sections.title: The Fall of Dun Garok
sections.body: Dun Garok is built against Thoradin's Wall in southeastern Hillsbrad. The fortified stronghold is held by disciplined mountaineers, skilled riflemen, and battle-hardened priests. To take it, Horde forces must break through those defenders and kill Captain Ironhill. His death breaks Ironforge's forward command in the region and leaves the remaining human enclaves isolated.

faq.q: Why are dwarves fighting in Hillsbrad?
aliases: why are there dwarves in hillsbrad
faq.answer: Ironforge sent its soldiers north to Dun Garok because the dwarves support the Alliance and want to aid the human survivors in Southshore and Hillsbrad against Forsaken expansion.
Dun Garok lies in southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills, built into the foundations of Thoradin's Wall.
Captain Ironhill commands Dun Garok's dwarven garrison and keeps its mountaineers organized and ready to fight in the region.
High Executor Darthalia, the Forsaken commander stationed at Tarren Mill, orders the attack on the dwarven garrison.

faq.q: What happens if Horde forces fail here?
faq.answer: Darthalia warns that failure will not be tolerated. Those who cannot break Dun Garok will be sent back to Tirisfal Glades to dig graves.

faq.q: Why is Dun Garok so difficult to assault?
faq.answer: Dun Garok is held by trained dwarven soldiers, rifle squads, and holy priests. They fight in tight formations inside the fortified underground and elevated bunker.

angles.text: Striking Dun Garok cuts off Ironforge's military reinforcements sent to aid the beleaguered humans of Southshore.
For the Forsaken, destroying the dwarven garrison secures southeastern Lordaeron and makes it harder for an Alliance vanguard to march south through Thoradin's Wall.
Dun Garok shows Ironforge's loyalty to its human allies. The dwarves endure the Forsaken siege to hold the northern frontier.
